title: Cast Iron vs. PVC in Drain, Waste, and Vent (DWV) Systems
description: Selecting the right material for DWV piping requires balancing installed cost, longevity, and acoustic performance. PVC is lightweight, corrosion-resistant, and cost-effective, making it ideal for standard residential applications. However, plastic pipes easily transmit fluid movement noise through building assemblies. Hubless cast iron piping, dense and heavy, provides superior sound dampening, making it the preferred choice for commercial structures and multi-family residential buildings where acoustic control is critical. Additionally, cast iron offers high fire resistance and low thermal expansion rates compared to plastic DWV materials. Understanding these material characteristics helps plumbers select the right pipe for specific job site requirements.
